reviews.review: Is it as good as the original trilogy, no? Is it still an above average role play experience. Yes. Real 6.5/10 flawed but enjoyable experience.

Aside from the female and male Krogan, and the a few of the new friendly aliens everyone's either annoying, or made feel really awkward talking with them/be around, I didn't even like either choice of main character they're both just whiny and everything about Andromeda just felt...forced, hell I flirted with Cora and got back in far too many words "er omg why does everyone assume I'm gay, I'm not gay, omg I'm not gay!!!"... mate, dude, sis a simple "no I'm alright thanks or sorry hon I don't tip the velvet" would have been fine, hell I couldn't even apologise for any uncomfortability caused, the awkwardness had me pull my neck back and raise an eyebrow, completely took me out of enjoying the game, as result I didn't put her in any of my teams and avoided talking to her throughout the 21hrs of game play, with Kaidan Alenko on the other hand, even though he fancied me a fair bit [throughout all three Mass Effects] I got to sit down and break bread with the man, to have a respectful, open discussion, to find a middle ground and remain solid friends even in the face total annihilation from the reapers.
Great game.  It got a lot of heat at launch, but I didn't play it then - they already had the kinks worked out by the time I started playing the game.

So, I do recommend the game, but let’s be clear:

    Is Mass Effect Andromeda a good Mass Effect game? No.
    Is Mass Effect Andromeda a good sci-fi and space exploration game? I guess… yeah.

The game got a lot of hate when it first released, and I can see why. Even after all the updates, eight years later it still has way too many bugs and just poorly developed things. If I compare this game as a whole to the Shepard trilogy, in terms of quality, it’s just bad. The story is decent, but the protagonist lacks in personality. And the faces—oh god, the faces. There isn’t a single cutscene where the character expressions don’t look weird. On top of that, I didn’t connect with any of the characters, and even the romances felt just empty.

But despite all that (which  I know are big issues in a game), why do I still recommend it? Well, as a space exploration game, it actually has some cool things to offer. The planets you visit are gorgeous, the sound design is nice, and there’s a lot of stuff to explore and side activities to do.

Also, the best thing about this game and probably the best feature in the whole franchise so far, is the insane amount of customization you get for skills and combos. There are tons of possible builds, making it feel like you can play dozens of different classes with the same character.

So, if you’re looking for a solid Mass Effect spin-off, I’m sorry to say this game lacks too much to be decent in that way. But if you just want a cool space-themed game, I think it’s worth giving a shot.
